title: The suffix table
goal: Every standalone ending stroke, its meaning, how it is built, how endings attach to a known word.

blocks.x: Source of truth: `rules/suffixes.toml`. A **standalone suffix stroke** is a continuation stroke (join key held) standing for an ending alone. Strike a stem, then the ending's stroke with `+` held: [[looks|HRAOBG/+-S]] is *look* then [[+-S]]. Usage: [lesson 10](#/lesson/10-endings), [The join key](#/ref/join-key).
Every suffix attaches on its own

Every suffix here is a **standalone dictionary entry on its starred chord**: the chord with `*` added to its first stroke, defined as an **exact attach** (`out/lyk/02-lyk-suffixes.json`): `+*D` is `{^}ed`, `+*G` is `{^}ing`, `+*EUZ/+-PL` is `{^}ism`. The star **forces the suffix, literally**: strike any word, then the starred chord, and the ending glues on exactly as written, with **no spelling rules** (no dropped *e*, no doubled consonant, no *y* to *i*), in any place of a run, never read as sounds or merged into a neighbour. *type* then `+*G` is *typeing*, *make* then `+*G` is *makeing*, *run* then `+*G` is *runing*, *walk* then `+*D` is *walked*; the plain chord is the spelled one: *type* then [[+-G]] is *typing*, *make* then [[+-G]] is *making*. The plain chord in the table ([[+-D]], [[+-G]], ...) is **not** an entry: [the solver](#/ref/fallback) reads it as the suffix or as part of the word's own sounds, whichever fits the whole run (*test* then [[+-D]] is *tested*; *prob* then [[+-BL]] is *probable*). Use the plain chord by default; use the star when you want the ending exactly as written (a misspelling on purpose, a name, a word the spelling rules get wrong) or the solver picks a whole word and you want the bare ending. A chord with its own star (`+*T` *th*, also the TH sound) has no forced form and is not an entry: the solver alone reads it as *-th* or TH, whichever spells the word (*four* then [[+*T]] is *fourth*; `H/+E/+HR/+*T` is *health*).

The engine must treat `+` as a join key and fall back to a continuation stroke's own entry: Keymux 1b9cf76 or later, with `extra_keys: ['+']` and `join_keys: ['+']` in the steno layer config (see [The join key](#/ref/join-key)). Older Keymux types a bare suffix stroke as its own word.
The rule

A suffix is a syllable: its sounds go through the same onset, vowel, coda, coda-cluster and vowel-coda tables as every syllable (see [Phonetic rules](#/ref/phonetic-rules)); no key combination is invented for suffixes. Then:

items: **Drop the vowel** when it is reducible (`AH`, `IH`, `ER`, the *-ly* spelling of `IY`, the *-ed* spelling of `OW`), **if the bare consonants still tell this suffix from every other suffix stroke.** Bare consonants read the same from a word's own ending or a suffix struck alone.
**Keep the vowel** when dropping it lands on a stroke another suffix holds (the *kept* table below).
A vowel outside the reducible list (`AY`, `UH`, `AO`, plain `IY`, `EY`, `AA`) stays.
A two-syllable suffix is two continuation strokes, each built by the same rule.

blocks.x: Endings built from table strokes
Some common endings need no row: they are table strokes in sequence.

items: **-ious, -eous**: the extra vowel before *-ous* is the plain IY of *-y*, so the ending is the two-stroke entry [[+AOE/+US]] (`{^ious}`; the two strokes apart would attach *y* then *ous*, "yous"): [[serious|S/+AOER/+AOE/+US]], [[various|SR/+AEUR/+AOE/+US]]. With no extra vowel (*gorgeous*, *courageous*, *religious*): plain [[+US]]: [[courageous|K-R/+AEUPBLG/+US]].

blocks.x: Not in the table: -graphy

**-graphy / -ography** (*biography*, *photography*, *geography*, *calligraphy*) has no standalone stroke. The schwa before *-graphy* takes a vowel key (`AH` or the spelled `AH.o` variant) depending on incidental spelling elsewhere in the word, which a standalone stroke cannot know; these words stay per-word through the normal rules.
A suffix stroke always reads right

Every single-stroke suffix chord above is known to the solver unconditionally, with or without a dictionary entry: a continuation stroke after the first of a run is also read as its suffix, never as its bare consonants. `+-D` after a stroke with no entry reads as *-ed*, never a bare "d"; a whole word that reads better still wins (`STKPW/+-D` reads *used*).

Matching stem guarantee: a run's first stroke, if already a placed single-stroke word, reads as that word's real text. `SKP/+-R` is *and* plus *-er*, read as "ander", not raw consonants plus a suffix.

Two-stroke suffixes read the same way: a joined stroke and the next one that together form one (`+EUZ/+-PL`) read as that suffix (*ism*) before either is sounded out alone. `KUB/+EUZ/+-PL` reads "cubism" with or without a dictionary entry. See [the solver](#/ref/fallback).
Backup stem-plus-suffix entries

The table also feeds the backup entries (full rules in [Syllables and folding](#/ref/syllables)). When a word's trailing syllable can be struck as a standalone continuation stroke and the sounds before it exactly match another placed word, the word gets a second entry: the stem's outline plus the suffix. *build* plus [[+-G]] also reaches *building*, whether or not that is *building*'s cheapest outline.

items: Exhaustive, run to a fixed point: every safe split is kept, and a backup can chain through another (*building* reaching *buildings* by adding [[+-S]] once *building* has an entry).

Two-syllable suffixes take part too, found by **spelling**, not sound: a word ending in the suffix's spelling (*cubism* ending in "ism") has its stem looked up by spelling and the suffix's two-stroke chord reused exactly. The second syllable's onset sometimes migrates onto the first suffix stroke, which sound cannot reproduce reliably.

blocks.x: Which endings join a stem you already know

Every ending here that attaches to a whole word is also a **backup join**: a word that is a placed word's spelling plus the ending (dropped *e*, doubled consonant, *y* to *i* all allowed) and sounds like it gets the stem's outline plus the ending's stroke as an extra entry. Examples: *fool* + [[+-RB]] for *foolish*, *art* + [[+EUFT]] for *artist*, *inform* + [[+AEUGS]] for *information*, *sail* + [[+-R]] for *sailor*, *sense* + [[+-BL]] for *sensible*.

Endings that join this way: *-s*, *-ed*, *-ing*, *-er/-or*, *-est*, *-ly*, *-y*, *-en*, *-ness*, *-ment*, *-able/-ible*, *-ful*, *-less* (the first thirteen, which also shape a word family's one-stroke outline), then *-ship*, *-hood*, *-ward*, *-ation*, *-ism*, *-ist*, *-ity*, *-ize*, *-ous*, *-ish*, *-ive*, *-age*, *-ic*, *-al* (these only add a way in). See [Every way to join a word](#/ref/ways-to-join).
